proposals.before: He habitually asked private audience with Chief Commandant of the Imperial Clan Ji An, let Ji An speak first, then added his own view; the ruler approved, adopted their advice, and drew Hong ever closer.
proposals.after: He habitually asked private audience with Chief Commandant of the Nobility Ji An, let Ji An speak first, then added his own view; the ruler approved, adopted their advice, and drew Hong ever closer.
proposals.reason: 主爵都尉 is the commandant overseeing noble ranks (爵), not the imperial clan office (宗正); "Imperial Clan" mistranslates the office title.

proposals.before: He constantly went with the chief commandant of the imperial clan, Ji An, to request a private audience; Ji An would speak first, and Hong would push his own views afterward; the emperor was always pleased, and whatever they said was all heard—by this he daily became more intimate and honored.
proposals.after: He constantly went with the chief commandant of the nobility, Ji An, to request a private audience; Ji An would speak first, and Hong would push his own views afterward; the emperor was always pleased, and whatever they said was all heard—by this he daily became more intimate and honored.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation as in the idiomatic field: 主爵都尉 concerns noble ranks, not the imperial clan.

proposals.before: In open court on the Tai rite he could not keep pace with his former pupil; afterward he conceded, "The throne really knows how to pick men."
proposals.after: When he arrived and debated the Feng and Shan rites with Kuan before the emperor, he could not match him; withdrawing he conceded, "The sovereign truly knows men."
proposals.reason: Chinese 議封禪 is debate of the Feng and Shan rites, not a vague 'Tai rite'; also names Kuan explicitly (與寬議) rather than only 'former pupil'.

proposals.before: Xuan continued the work, revived the six arts, and called forth the brilliant: Confucians such as Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, and the rest; stylists Liu Xiang and Wang Bao; ministers Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, Du Yannian; magistrates Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang—each left a mark the age remembers.
proposals.after: Xuan continued the work, revived the six arts, and called forth the brilliant: Confucians Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; stylists Liu Xiang and Wang Bao; ministers Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, Du Yannian; magistrates Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang—each left a mark the age remembers.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents 'and the rest' while omitting the named Confucians 夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖、尹更始 present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Emperor Xuan inherited the line, continued the great enterprise, also lectured on the six arts, summoned and selected the flourishing and unusual, while Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiasheng Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning, Liu Xiang and Wang Bao distinguished themselves in literary composition, among generals and ministers Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian, in governing the people Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang and the like—all had meritorious deeds narrated in their age.
proposals.after: Emperor Xuan inherited the line, continued the great enterprise, also lectured on the six arts, summoned and selected the flourishing and unusual, while Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning, Liu Xiang and Wang Bao distinguished themselves in literary composition, among generals and ministers Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian, in governing the people Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang and the like—all had meritorious deeds narrated in their age.
proposals.reason: Literal romanization 'Xiasheng Sheng' mistranscribes 夏侯勝, which is Xiahou Sheng.

decisions.after: He habitually sought private audience together with Ji An, Commandant of Nobility Ranks. Ji An would speak first, and Hong would then add his own view; the emperor was always pleased and accepted everything they said, so Hong grew more intimate and honored by the day.
decisions.reason: 主爵都尉 is Commandant of Nobility Ranks, not an imperial-clan office; the revision also restores the sentence's sequence and established title style.

decisions.after: He regularly sought private audience together with Ji An, Commandant of Nobility Ranks; Ji An spoke first and Hong developed the argument afterward. The emperor was always pleased and accepted everything they said, and by this Hong daily grew more intimate and honored.
decisions.reason: 主爵都尉 is Commandant of Nobility Ranks, not an imperial-clan office; the revision corrects the title and preserves the literal sequence.

decisions.after: When Chu Da reached court and debated the Feng and Shan sacrifices with Kuan before the emperor, he could not match him. Afterward he conceded, "The sovereign truly knows men."
decisions.reason: 與寬議封禪於上前 names Kuan and the Feng and Shan sacrifices and places the debate before the emperor; the original's 'Tai rite' is invented.

decisions.after: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too expounded the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men. Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction for their writing; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; and among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All left achievements celebrated in their age.
decisions.reason: The original replaces 夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖、尹更始 with invented 'and the rest'; the revision restores every named category and divides the long catalogue into readable English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蕭望之、梁丘賀、夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖，尹更始以儒術進

decisions.after: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too discussed the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men: Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction through literary composition; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All had achievements recounted in their age.
decisions.reason: The revision corrects 夏侯勝 to Xiahou Sheng and replaces the unreadable run-on with a clear catalogue that preserves every person and category.
